title: Your Metre
text: Measure the Sight, an homage to the 2015 exhibition on units. Start with your own body: a metre on the lobby floor and, beside it, a shaku, 10/33 of a metre, once taken from the forearm.

title: The Tall Pane
text: Glass runs from this floor to the roof, held by solid steel mullions up to about 11.7 m tall. On the floor is a sundial set for Tokyo, 35.67° north. Before clocks, a shadow measured the day.

title: Basic Units
text: Same size, different weight. One litre of water weighs one kilogram. Six identical bags hold six different units, and a thousand 3.75 g discs make one kan.

title: From 10 to 100
text: Ten plywood cubes, from ten centimetres to one metre. Walk past them and your sense of length begins to recalibrate.

title: How Big Is This Building?
text: Gallery 2 is 443 m², about 134 tsubo or 273 tatami. A full doubles tennis court, 23.77 by 10.97 m, fits inside with room to spare.

title: At 1:100
text: The same building on a table. From the garden it is a low folded roof; at this scale you see that four-fifths of it lies underground.

title: Bodies and Tools
text: A pendulum 0.994 m long beats once a second. In the 1790s it nearly became the definition of the metre.

title: 54 Metres of Steel
text: The roof plate at 1:10 in length, but at its true 16 mm thickness: one folded sheet, 54 m long, welded on site. It moves by about 30 mm between winter and summer.
